text:
Tessa Morgan: quick design review request for RBAC v2 role management screens + copy for permission warnings/denied actions. Figma here (internal): https://figma.com/file/RBACv2-RoleMgmt-IA?node-id=1182%3A44210 — would love eyes esp on “you don’t have permission” states.

Marissa Cole: looking now. overall layout feels good. question: are we committing to default roles-only in v1? some of the copy mentions “custom roles”.

Naomi Feldman: +1. for GA1 we’re shipping default roles + limited “role sets” for enterprise, but not full custom roles editor. would prefer copy doesn’t imply they can create new roles.

Tessa Morgan: yep good catch. I can swap “custom roles” language to “additional roles” / “contact support” depending on tier.

Felix Schneider: jumping in on denied-action UI. I like the pattern of inline callout on the page rather than a toast. toast gets missed and doesn’t explain what to do.

Chloe Martin: from console backend side: we will return 403 with reason codes (from PR_18451) like `AUTHZ_DENY_MISSING_PERMISSION` + `required_permission` string. we can surface that if we want, but we should be careful not to leak internal action names verbatim.

Jada Williams: agreed. we can show a human string + “Details” accordion with the exact permission only when user has Security Admin maybe? (or when they click “copy error details”)?

Marcus Lin: security preference: don’t show raw permission identifiers by default in UI (helps attackers enumerate). but for debugging we do need a way for admins/support to get it.

Felix Schneider: what about “Request access” / “Contact an admin” CTA that pre-fills a message including the permission string, but only reveals it once you click copy? (still accessible to any user though)

Marcus Lin: copying the permission string into a message is fine. just don’t print it on-screen automatically.

Elliot Price: docs angle: we need consistent phrasing across console + docs. “You don’t have permission” is fine, but we should name which role can grant it: Org Admin / Security Admin etc.

Tessa Morgan: current copy draft on denied page:
- Title: “You don’t have access to this page”
- Body: “Ask an administrator to grant you the required role.”
- CTA: “View roles in your org” (if you can see role list) or “Contact your admin”
Thoughts?

Marissa Cole: “administrator” is vague. could be “Org Admin” specifically (and “Security Admin” for some things). can we map required_permission -> suggested roles?

Chloe Martin: technically yes: we’ll have a mapping table in the frontend or returned from the backend. but we need that mapping to be maintained. otherwise it’ll drift.

Naomi Feldman: please don’t block on a perfect mapping. could start with generic “Org Admin” and tighten later. also separation-of-duties: Billing Admin should NOT be told to ask Billing Admin for access to SSO settings, etc.

Jada Williams: UI option: show “This action requires an admin role” + link to “Learn about roles” (docs). for certain pages we know the right role: Billing pages -> Billing Admin; SSO -> Security Admin/Org Admin.

Felix Schneider: on the role assignment screen itself, we need warnings when granting high-risk roles. I see the yellow warning in Figma (“Security Admin can manage SSO and audit exports”). I’d make it more explicit: “This role can change authentication settings for the org.”

Marcus Lin: +1 and add “Use least privilege” nudge. also for Support/Impersonation role, we should never show it in normal UI (internal only). make sure it’s not visible in screenshots.

Tessa Morgan: yep, Support/Impersonation not in UI. only in internal admin tooling.

Marissa Cole: for denied *actions* inside a page (e.g., user can view billing but not edit payment method), what do we want? disable button w/ tooltip? or hide?

Jada Williams: prefer disabled + tooltip. hiding makes it harder to understand capabilities and increases support tickets (“where is the button”).

Felix Schneider: disabled w/ tooltip copy should be short. e.g. “Requires Billing Admin role.” and include “Learn more” link.

Chloe Martin: just note: not all endpoints will be “view allowed but edit denied” at first. some pages might 403 the whole route if the backend check is at route-level.

Naomi Feldman: for MVP, route-level denies are ok. but for common pages like billing, the view/edit split is a good enterprise expectation.

Tessa Morgan: ok. I’ll update patterns:
1) Page-level deny state: banner card with “Contact Org Admin” + “Copy details” (includes request id + reason code, not raw permission unless expanded)
2) Inline action deny: disabled control + tooltip “Requires <role>”
3) Role grant warning modal: explicit capability bullets + “I understand” checkbox for Security Admin

Marcus Lin: re: “Copy details” — include request ID + timestamp + policy version. that’s useful for audit/debug, and not sensitive.

Chloe Martin: we can return `x-request-id` and `policy_version` in response headers (or body) consistently. I’ll check with Kaitlyn/Jordan but should be doable.

Elliot Price: can you also avoid “Contact support” in the default deny state unless it’s actually a support flow. enterprise will want self-serve: “Ask your Org Admin to assign a role in Settings → Access.”

Marissa Cole: +1. also add a non-blocking note on role list page: “Roles are managed by Org Admins.” Some users will land there from deny CTA.

Tessa Morgan: got it. I’ll push an updated Figma pass today and drop here for final skim. thanks all :thumbsup:

Felix Schneider: :thumbsup: once you update, I’ll sanity-check empty states + tooltip sizing.

Marcus Lin: thanks. please also make sure the warning color hierarchy works for dark mode (we’ve had contrast issues).

Tessa Morgan: noted. I’ll run it through contrast checker + ping you if anything is borderline.
